venue: Swachh Bharat Diwas event, Sabarmati Riverfront, Ahmedabad, Gujarat
quote_english: In 60 months, 600 million people have been given access to toilets (as quoted by Al Jazeera); he declared India open-defecation free.
summary: The ODF label rests on government village-level verification; independent surveys and later official data showed continued open defecation and incomplete toilet access, though toilet coverage rose sharply.

evidence.title: Modi declares India open defecation free, claim questioned
evidence.key_figure: RICE survey of 3,235 households in 4 states (2014, 2018): toilet access 37% to 71%, but 23% of toilet owners still defecated in the open; World Bank: over 300 million still practised OD in 2017

evidence.title: NFHS-5 2019-21 improved sanitation facility, as summarised by Down To Earth
evidence.key_figure: About 70% of households used an improved sanitation facility (about 65% rural), up from 49% in NFHS-4; article cautions against taking figures at face value

govt_response.title: Government position as reported by Al Jazeera
govt_response.summary: Officials said over 100 million of 120 million planned toilets were built, villages were verified ODF, and the urban target was 100% achieved; the PM said the focus now shifts to sustained use.

analysis:
On 2 October 2019 the PM declared India open-defecation free after the Swachh Bharat Mission built more than 100 million household toilets. ODF under the mission means no visible faeces in a village and access to a toilet, verified by the state, not zero open defecation by every person.

Independent evidence points to a gap. The RICE survey found 23% of toilet owners in four northern states still defecated in the open, and NFHS-5 (2019-21) found about 70% of households using an improved sanitation facility (about 65% rural). NFHS measures use of improved facilities, a stricter standard than ODF verification, so the figures are not directly comparable.

The gains are real: coverage rose from about 39% in 2014 by the government's count.
